alerts.reason: Black Knight reported lower mortgage origination volumes as rates rose after a prolonged period of elevated refinancing (C). I forecast Q3 consolidated revenue growth above -5% and a Q4 decline of at least 5% as fewer originations generate transaction revenue. The timing is uncertain because the filing does not quantify revenue tied to originations.

nLIGHT’s first-half revenue fell 4.0% year over year, from $130.5 million to $125.3 million. Product sales outside China rose and partly offset declines in China sales and development revenue (A). I expect that offset to keep Q3 above -5%, with weaker demand and delayed customer capital spending pushing the Q4 decline to at least 5% (B).

Matson’s Q2 Ocean Transportation revenue grew 53.6%, supporting a forecast for consolidated revenue growth above -5% in Q3 (A). Hawaii container volume had already fallen 1.5% year over year, and Matson cited lower retail-related demand (B, C). I forecast a Q4 consolidated decline of at least 5% if that weakness spreads beyond Hawaii.

Black Knight’s reported revenue growth eased from 10.72% in March to 9.19% in June, leaving room for September to stay above -5%. Mortgage originations were already falling as rates rose after a prolonged refinancing boom (C). I forecast that lower origination volumes against elevated prior-year volumes will pull December-quarter revenue down at least 5% year over year.

nLIGHT’s June revenue fell 11.99% year over year during a roughly two-month Shanghai plant closure (D). I forecast a September rebound above -5% as that temporary disruption eases, followed by a December decline of at least 5%. Lower China product sales, declining development revenue and customers delaying capital spending support the renewed decline (A, B).

Matson’s consolidated revenue growth slowed from 63.74% in March to 44.14% in June. Ocean Transportation revenue still rose 53.6%, but Hawaii container volume fell 1.5% as retail demand weakened (A–C). I forecast September growth above -5% and a December decline of at least 5% if the weakness in retail freight spreads beyond Hawaii.
